body:
_Migrated from issue #1319, filed 2026-08-03._

Noted during #1316 and filed rather than widened into it.

## What

`cps/web.py` resolves a bookmark with an epub/kepub sibling fallback (`cps/web.py:3328-3333`), so the classic reader still finds a position saved under the other of the two formats. The SPA's bookmark GET in `cps/api/reader.py` has no such fallback — it looks up the exact format only.

## Effect

When the served format switches between `epub` and `kepub` (on-demand conversion, a format being added or removed, or Kobo-oriented settings changing what is offered), the two readers can resolve to different `ub.Bookmark` rows for the same book. The user sees their place in one reader and an older place — or none — in the other, with no indication why.

Orthogonal to cross-device progress, which is keyed by book rather than format and so is unaffected.

## Shape of the fix

Give the API route the same sibling resolution the classic route has, from one shared helper rather than a second copy — the two drifting is what produced this. A test should pin that a bookmark saved as `epub` is found when the served format is `kepub` and the reverse.
title: SPA and classic readers can land on different bookmark rows when the served format switches to kepub
